brainrot.name: brainrot
world: ordinary public places with one impossible rule
tiny miniature worlds hidden inside normal objects
overly serious workplaces for ridiculous creatures
surreal kitchens, bathrooms, bedrooms, and convenience stores
dramatic fantasy environments used for trivial problems
liminal spaces that behave like broken reality
protagonists: a completely ordinary person trapped in an impossible situation
an animal acting with eerie human intelligence
an animal with an absurd human job
a creature that cannot exist, behaving with total confidence
a person whose shadow, reflection, or body part acts independently
an animal that becomes enormous or tiny while the world stays normal
a swarm of identical living things moving as one
a badly disguised monster trying to act normal
comedy_types: a mundane task treated like an extreme emergency
a tiny consequence becoming visually enormous
an object behaving according to a ridiculous hidden law
a bizarre reveal that reinterprets the entire shot
physical comedy with surreal cause and effect
a normal person reacting calmly to impossible nonsense
prompt_guidance: Start with a recognizable situation, then corrupt one fundamental rule of reality.
Make the first visual readable but immediately wrong in a specific way.
Use one dominant absurd premise and escalate it into a clear visual payoff.
Favor concrete, filmable actions over abstract weirdness.
Use deadpan seriousness for ridiculous events whenever possible.
End on an image that is stranger than the setup, not merely louder or more violent.
Make the idea feel like a lost internet meme from a universe with broken physics.

instructions: Generate one original Brainrot concept suitable for a short vertical video.
Every concept must contain a concrete visual hook that is strange within the first image.
Use one dominant impossible premise, then escalate it once into a memorable payoff.
The result should be easy to visualize but difficult to explain logically.
Make the concept feel unhinged, cursed, surreal, and meme-worthy rather than merely silly.
Do not reuse familiar gravity-defying cats, generic dancing animals, or standard cartoon accidents.
The main character must be ALIVE: a person, animal, insect, sea creature, or monster. Never make an inanimate object the main character.
Push every idea for genuine WOW factor: the viewer should gasp or laugh out loud within the first second.
creative_directions: Combine unrelated domains: bureaucracy with monsters, fine dining with household objects, sports with food, surgery with toys, or luxury fashion with trash.
Use scale violations, impossible anatomy, objects with jobs, creatures with official titles, and environments with personalities.
Let a completely normal character calmly accept something visually impossible.
Use realistic cinematic detail to make the nonsense feel more serious and funnier.
Prefer a premise that can be summarized as: 'Why is that thing doing that?'
Use physically filmable wording: name what is visible, what moves, and where it ends.
Avoid abstract labels such as sentient charts, world collapse, or emotional concepts without a visible action.
Avoid ambiguous actions such as processing a paper cut; show the character stamping, carrying, opening, folding, or physically manipulating a concrete object.
Keep the prompt to one dominant subject and no more than one or two supporting objects.
Use only one transformation or one physical escalation; do not chain multiple transformations in the same shot.
End with a concrete final pose, object, or location that the video model can clearly render.
Prioritize stop-scrolling visual absurdity: unexpected legs, eyes, mouths, hands, anatomy, jobs, or behavior are better than merely floating, flying, levitating, or breaking gravity.
Objects may appear, but only as props, clothing, food, or the absurd element a LIVING main character interacts with.
Chase genuine WOW factor: impossible biology, living swarms, body parts with their own agendas, or reveals that recontextualize the whole shot.
absurdity_families: impossible biology: a living body grows, opens, splits, or produces something impossible
living scale violation: an animal or person becomes enormous or tiny while everything else stays normal
body-part independence: a shadow, reflection, hand, or smile detaches and follows its own agenda
animal intelligence: an animal calmly performs a complex human ritual, job, or ceremony
creature cameo: an impossible creature appears in public and everyone reacts normally
living swarm: one living thing multiplies into dozens of identical copies that act together
broken physics around a living subject: gravity, reflections, doors, or weather obey a ridiculous rule affecting them
reality reveal: something ordinary opens to reveal an impossible living world
mundane escalation: a trivial task by a living character spirals into a physically impossible emergency
diversity_guidance: Avoid repeating the same joke structure.
Avoid repeating gravity tricks, dancing animals, falling objects, and generic popping or exploding gags.
Do not use the same subject-object pairing twice.
Change the emotional tone, scale, setting, and type of impossible rule between concepts.
wow_factor_guidance: The concept should make a viewer gasp, laugh out loud, or ask 'what am I watching' within the first second.
Escalate until the final image is ten times stranger than the setup.
Combine two things nobody would ever put together, then treat the combination as completely normal.
Use dramatic cinematic energy for something utterly ridiculous.
End on a twist image that makes the viewer want to rewatch immediately.
living_subject_rules: The main character must be ALIVE: a person, animal, insect, sea creature, or monster.
Inanimate objects may never be the main character; they can only appear as props, clothing, food, or the absurd element the living character interacts with.
When an object misbehaves, show a living character noticing or reacting to it.
